summary: Improve alert triage, typology design, and monitoring controls with practical AML exercises. Explore the course and review the outline.
lede: Transaction monitoring training helps AML and compliance professionals assess monitoring controls, review alerts, and document investigation decisions. Participants practise analyzing alert data, prioritizing cases, developing typologies and thresholds, and building quality-assurance and model-risk records using synthetic examples. It also covers FATF risk-based principles, Wolfsberg guidance, and operational oversight of digital queues and automated monitoring controls.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with AML obligations and need practical methods for transaction monitoring, alert handling, investigation quality, and reporting.
modules: Alert Triage in FATF Risk-Based Monitoring
Model Risk Controls and STR Case Management
prerequisites: Prior working knowledge of AML obligations and transaction-monitoring operations is expected. No programming is required. Bring a laptop with spreadsheet software; the exercises use synthetic records and spreadsheet-based analysis.
